questions.q: According to Kent, a remedy that produces new symptoms in the patient was:
opts: only partially similar, so the case needs restudy
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Kent's ninth observation: new symptoms mean the remedy was not well chosen.

questions.q: A type I (alpha) error in hypothesis testing is:
opts: rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true
accepting a null hypothesis that is actually false
questions.why: Type I error is a false positive conclusion (rejecting a true null hypothesis); accepting a false null hypothesis is a type II error.

questions.q: A Colles' fracture is a fracture of the:
questions.why: From a fall on the outstretched hand.

questions.q: Under standard pre-anaesthetic fasting guidelines for an elective adult operation, clear fluids may be taken up to:
questions.why: Usual rules: clear fluids 2 h, breast milk 4 h, light meal or non-human milk 6 h.

questions.q: In hepatitis B infection, the serum marker indicating active viral replication and high infectivity is:
questions.why: HBeAg correlates with high levels of HBV DNA and infectivity; seroconversion to anti-HBe indicates reduced replication.

questions.q: On abdominal ultrasonography, fatty liver typically appears as a liver with:
opts: A shrunken nodular outline with ascites
questions.why: Fat in hepatocytes increases reflectivity, so the liver looks brighter than the kidney cortex; a small nodular liver with ascites suggests cirrhosis.

questions.q: The first heart sound is produced by closure of the:
questions.why: S1 marks the start of ventricular systole.

questions.q: Red blood cell casts in urine indicate:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. WBC casts suggest pyelonephritis.

questions.q: Knerr's Repertory is an index to:
Which of these is a purposive repertory dealing with a single region?
